episodeTitle.en: Leveraging growth advisors, mastering SEO, and honing your craft | Luc Levesque (Shopify, Meta)
episodeTitle.zh: 借助增长顾问、精通SEO并磨练技艺 | 卢克·莱维斯克（Shopify、Meta）

guestBioOfficial.en: Luc Levesque is Chief Growth Officer at Shopify and has advised companies like Canva, Twitter, Pinterest, and Patreon on growth and product strategy. Previously he served as an executive at TripAdvisor, where he built and led the growth team that helped it become the world’s largest travel site. Luc was then recruited by Mark Zuckerberg to Facebook, where he was an executive and held senior product and engineering leadership roles. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Why you need to become world-class at hiring
guestBioOfficial.zh: 卢克·莱维斯克（Luc Levesque）是Shopify的首席增长官，曾为Canva、Twitter、Pinterest和Patreon等公司提供增长和产品策略咨询。此前，他在TripAdvisor担任高管，组建并领导了推动该平台成为全球最大旅游网站的增长团队。随后，马克·扎克伯格将卢克招入Facebook，担任高管并担任高级产品和工程领导职务。在本期节目中，我们探讨了：•为何你需要在招聘方面达到世界级水准

title.en: Leveraging growth advisors, mastering SEO, and honing your craft | Luc Levesque (Shopify, Meta)
title.zh: 借助增长顾问、精通SEO并磨练技艺 | 卢克·莱维斯克（Shopify、Meta）

summary.en: Luc makes the case for hiring a great growth advisor, arguing that the right person at the right time can change a company's trajectory with a single sentence and deliver 100% to 1000%+ lifts. He shares how to decide when you need an advisor, how to structure the relationship, and what to look for in one. A large part of the conversation is devoted to SEO as a growth channel—who it suits, how to think about it, and how everything is about to change with AI tools like Bard and ChatGPT. He also offers unexpected advice on self-reflection, building routines, and cold plunges, plus memorable stories from working alongside Zuckerberg and the relentless 'impact' culture at Facebook.
summary.zh: Luc 力陈聘请一位优秀增长顾问的价值，他认为在对的时机遇到对的人，一句话就能改变公司的走向，带来 100% 乃至 1000% 以上的提升。他分享了如何判断自己是否需要顾问、如何设计合作关系，以及该看重顾问的哪些特质。对话的很大篇幅都集中在 SEO 这一增长渠道上——它适合谁、该怎么思考，以及随着 Bard、ChatGPT 这类 AI 工具出现，一切将如何改变。他还给出了关于自我反思、建立日常节奏和冷水浴的意外建议，并讲述了一些与 Zuckerberg 共事、以及 Facebook 那种对“影响力（impact）”近乎偏执的文化里的难忘故事。
